summary: Configured a four-node distributed MinIO EC:2 cluster with trusted TLS S3 on port 9000. The requested object exists, one-member failover and automatic healing passed, and every node survived an isolated OS reboot. Node1 administration is available with `sudo -H mc … infra`.
actions_performed: Configured storage-network aliases for node1–node4 on 10.100.245.10–13.
Installed verified MinIO binaries and protected credentials/TLS identities.
Configured persistent data volumes and enabled systemd services on all nodes.
Verified reads and writes while node4 was unavailable, followed by automatic rejoin and healing.
Restarted every node sequentially and verified changed boot identities, service recovery, data persistence, and full cluster health.

evidence.requirement: Distributed MinIO over the dedicated storage network with trusted TLS on port 9000
evidence.summary: Storage aliases resolve to the managed-node addresses; MinIO reports four online members, and every node verifies TLS and cluster readiness.
The protected `infra` alias successfully performs authenticated administration and reports four online drives with EC:2.
Proves creation of `infra-data`, 25-byte `proof.txt`, and exact content `distributed-storage-ready`.

evidence.requirement: Read/write availability with one storage member unavailable
evidence.summary: Node4 was inactive while the 3/4-member cluster remained ready, read `proof.txt`, and wrote/read `during-outage.txt`.

evidence.requirement: Automatic member rejoin and healing with current data
evidence.summary: Node4 automatically rejoined as the fourth online drive, served the outage-time object, and subsequently acquired its missing local erasure metadata and data part without manual healing.
Healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service/mount/data with four drives online.
Healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, direct data recovery, and restored four-drive membership.
Healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, direct data recovery, and restored four-drive membership.
Healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, direct data recovery, and final four-drive membership.
All four nodes are active and enabled, have persistent ext4 mounts, listen on port 9000, return TLS health 200, and serve both authenticated objects.
